From the docs, here's what the keyless install will do once it can run:

1. `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.734.0`
2. `gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding` sets up keyless local memory, with no API keys.
3. `printf 'Y\n' | hermes mcp add gbrain --env GBRAIN_HOME=$HOME --connect-timeout 60 --command $(which gbrain) --args serve --surface starter --advertise verbs`, then `hermes mcp test gbrain`.
4. `gbrain setup hermes --instructions-only` adds one marked block to `$HERMES_HOME/SOUL.md` after your existing identity text, which stays first and unchanged.
5. Check: `gbrain doctor --only harness_wiring --json`, then remember a test marker, recall it in a new process, and forget it.

Search mode: with no keys, init normally applies `conservative`. You can switch any time with `gbrain config set search.mode <mode>`. Here is the choice, with the docs' cost table quoted exactly:

    Estimated downstream input cost of the retrieved payload @ 10K queries/mo:

                      Haiku 5.5     Sonnet 5.5    Opus 5.5
                      ($0.10/M in)  ($2/M in)     ($4/M in)
      conservative    $4/mo         $80/mo        $160/mo
      balanced        $10/mo        $200/mo       $400/mo
      tokenmax        $20/mo        $400/mo       $800/mo

      Assumed payload per query: conservative 4K, balanced 10K, tokenmax 20K tokens.
      Scales linearly: x10 for 100K queries/mo, /10 for 1K. 200x corner-to-corner spread.
      Embedding, reranking and query expansion are separate provider charges.

  1) conservative: 4K budget, up to 10 chunks, no reranker. This is the keyless default.
  2) balanced: 12K budget, 25 chunks, reranked.
  3) tokenmax: no budget limit, 50 chunks, reranked. The docs recommend it when a chat model key is set.
